record.paper_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
record.original_question: How should federated-learning systems communicate privacy benefits and limitations to ordinary users, model user privacy preferences, decide who sets privacy and security parameters, and incorporate individual choices about desired privacy levels or allowable inferences?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a federated learning system in which a central server coordinates the training of a shared model across a population of clients $\mathcal{U} = \{u_1, \dots, u_N\}$, each holding private local data $D_i$. The system applies a privacy mechanism $\mathcal{M}$ (e.g., a $(\varepsilon_i,\delta_i)$-differentially private mechanism, secure aggregation, or a combination) with privacy parameters $	heta_i \in \Theta$ that may vary per user. Each user $u_i$ has a (possibly unknown) privacy preference modeled as a utility function $V_i : \Theta 	imes \mathcal{I} 	o \mathbb{R}$, where $\mathcal{I}$ denotes the set of inferences an adversary could potentially make from released information; the user wishes to permit some inferences (those useful to the learning task) while disallowing others.

Develop a principled framework that simultaneously addresses the following:

1. (Communication of guarantees) Define a function $C : \Theta 	o \mathcal{R}$, where $\mathcal{R}$ is a space of human-interpretable representations, that conveys to a non-expert user both the privacy benefits and limitations of $\mathcal{M}$ with parameters $	heta_i$, in a way that is provably faithful to the underlying mathematical guarantee.

2. (Modeling preferences) Construct a model class $\{V_i^{\widehat{}} : i \in \mathcal{U}\}$ that approximates each user's true preference $V_i$ from a feasible elicitation procedure, with quantitative guarantees on approximation error.

3. (Parameter setting authority) Specify a decision protocol $\pi$ that determines whether $	heta_i$ is set by the user, by the service provider, by a third party, or by a combination, optimizing an explicit social welfare or game-theoretic objective $W(	heta_1,\dots,	heta_N)$ that balances utility of the learned model against per-user privacy loss.

4. (Incorporating individual choices) Design an aggregation/training algorithm $\mathcal{A}$ that takes heterogeneous user-chosen privacy levels $\{	heta_i\}$ and allowed-inference sets $\{I_i \subseteq \mathcal{I}\}$ as input, and produces a model whose privacy guarantees with respect to each user $u_i$ provably respect $	heta_i$ and $I_i$, while maximizing expected model utility.

Provide existence, optimality, or impossibility results for such a framework $(C, \{V_i^{\widehat{}}\}, \pi, \mathcal{A})$.
artifact.status_search_result: This is a long-standing open research direction in federated learning, spanning differential privacy, mechanism design, and HCI. As of 2026 no unified mathematical framework addresses all four sub-problems with provable guarantees; partial progress exists on heterogeneous/personalized differential privacy and on privacy-utility tradeoff mechanisms, but communicating guarantees to users and eliciting preferences remain largely unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
status_evidence.snippet: Lists user privacy perception and personalized privacy as open problems in federated learning.
status_evidence.claim: The questions are explicitly framed as open problems.

status_evidence.title: Heterogeneous Differential Privacy
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress on heterogeneous per-user privacy parameters exists but does not address user communication or preference elicitation.
